answer: One defence is vouching with liability: a new agent only enters after an established one stakes part of its own bond behind it, so the network grows like a reef built on older coral. If the newcomer is later proven to be a sock puppet, the voucher is slashed too, so every fake identity must mirror a real loss for a real sponsor. An attacker cannot mint a thousand opal-bright personas cheaply: each one needs a sponsor willing to risk collateral, and the price climbs as burned vouchers lose their standing.
